title: Five-colored parakeet on a blossoming apricot tree

source.label: Wikipedia: Huizong, a painter, poet and calligrapher, reigned until the Jin conquest of 1126
Wikipedia: “The primary subjects of his paintings are birds and flowers. Among his works is Five-Colored Parakeet…”

highlight.text: They represent a new stage in the development of flower- and bird-painting; their absolute fidelity to nature is … combined with a refinement of design and colouring that sometimes almost becomes prettiness. It is an art which sought perfection within rather narrow limits and consequently became a classic model for later generations.

work.text: The primary subjects of his paintings are birds and flowers. Among his works is Five-Colored Parakeet on Blossoming Apricot Tree.

These highly finished and delicately coloured pictures are masterpieces of their kind, but they are evidently done by an artist who has had his whole attention concentrated on the minute representation of natural models with no inclination to transpose the motives in an expressionistic sense.

matters.text: The painting is one of Huizong’s “three perfections”: beside the bird he wrote, in his own Slender Gold hand, a poem about it and signed it. Picture, verse and writing were all meant to be read as the emperor’s.
